","width":500,"height":460,"source":"Cropped figure from user-supplied textbook PDF","cropPdfPoints":[295,510,545,740],"status":"figure number and printed page checked in PDF; crop visually reviewed by montage"},{"id":"figure-3-13","headingId":"bp14-m3-1-h06","number":"3.13","title":"Subcortical brain structures","printedPage":75,"pdfPage":93,"alt":"Excerpt from Figure 3.13 of Kalat Biological Psychology, showing subcortical brain structures.","image":"data:image/webp;base64,","width":1012,"height":518,"source":"Cropped figure from user-supplied textbook PDF","cropPdfPoints":[69,65,575,324],"status":"figure number and printed page checked in PDF; crop visually reviewed by montage"}]},{"id":"bp14-m3-2","chapterId":"bp14-ch03","moduleId":"bp14-m3-2","moduleNumber":"3.2","title":"The Cerebral Cortex","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":81,"printedEnd":90,"pdfStart":99,"pdfEnd":108,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cerebral cortex has layers, columns, and interconnected regions. Its occipital, parietal, temporal, and frontal lobes contribute to different functions, but complex behavior depends on communication across areas."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module discusses the prefrontal cortex and the limitations of assigning a complete mental ability to just one location. Use the connections among areas to think about the binding problem and coordinated processing."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-1","text":"Cortex: layers, columns, and connections"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cerebral cortex is the folded outer part of the cerebral hemispheres. Its neurons are organized in layers and interconnected local circuits, and groups of cells can share response properties in columns. The amount and arrangement of cortical tissue vary among species and individuals. The cortex is highly differentiated, but no area acts independently: communication among regions is central to almost every complex function. White-matter connections are as important as familiar gray-matter regions."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-2","text":"The four lobes"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The occipital lobe is particularly involved in vision; the parietal lobe contributes to body-related sensation and spatial processing; the temporal lobe participates in hearing, object recognition, and aspects of memory; and frontal regions contribute to movement, planning, and control. These are broad associations, not rigid boundaries. A perceptual or cognitive task typically recruits multiple areas, and damage effects depend on the location and extent of injury as well as connections disrupted."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-3","text":"Prefrontal cortex and behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Prefrontal regions help maintain goals, regulate actions, inhibit unsuitable responses, and organize behavior over time. Historical prefrontal lobotomies illustrate the severe human cost of intervening in brain systems before understanding their roles and risks. Modern research asks not just whether frontal cortex is active during a task but which processes and connections are necessary. Inhibition is a genuine achievement: deciding not to act can require neural control as much as deciding to move."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-2-study-4","text":"Avoid the localization trap"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It is useful to associate functions with brain areas, but it is inaccurate to claim that one small cortical patch uniquely contains a skill such as 'thinking' or 'personality.' Sensory information is processed through distributed hierarchies and recurrent communication. When interpreting a scan or lesion, distinguish involvement from exclusivity. Cortical specialization and cooperation are simultaneously true."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h01","text":"Organization of the Cerebral Cortex"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The microscopic structure of neurons varies from one cortical area to another, as does their density per volume .","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In humans and most other mammals, the cerebral cortex contains up to six distinct laminae , layers of cell bodies parallel to the surface of the cortex (Figure 3.20).","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The laminae vary in prominence from one part of the cortex to another, and a given lamina may be absent from certain areas.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Lamina IV, which receives sensory information, is prominent in the sensory areas of the cortex but absent from the motor cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Lamina V, which sends long axons to the spinal cord, is thickest in the motor cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Layer I, with many axons and dendrites but few cells, is a site for many connections, including those that are essential for learning.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The cells of the cortex are also organized into columns of cells perpendicular to the laminae.","sourcePrintedPage":82,"sourcePdfPage":100,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h02","text":"The Occipital Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We group the areas of cortex into four lobes named for the skull bones that lie over them: occipital, parietal, temporal, and frontal.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The posterior pole of the occipital lobe is called the primary visual cortex , or striate cortex , because of its striped appearance in cross section.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Damage in the striate cortex causes cortical blindness in the related part of the visual field.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"damage to the striate cortex of the right hemisphere causes blindness in the left visual field (the left side of the world from the viewer’s perspective).","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People who experience eye damage become blind, but if they have an intact occipital cortex and previous visual experience, they can still have visual imagery and visual dreams .","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h03","text":"The Parietal Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parietal lobe lies between the occipital lobe and the central sulcus , a deep groove in the surface of the cortex (Figure 3.23).","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The area just posterior to the central sulcus, the postcentral gyrus , or primary somatosensory cortex , receives sensations from touch receptors, muscle-stretch receptors, and joint receptors.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain surgeons sometimes use only local anesthesia, anesthetizing the scalp but leaving the brain awake.","sourcePrintedPage":83,"sourcePdfPage":101,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Two of the bands receive mostly light-touch information, one receives deep-pressure information, and one receives a combination of both .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Information about touch and body location is important not only for its own sake but also for interpreting visual and auditory information.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parietal lobe monitors the information about eye, head, and body positions and passes it on to brain areas that control movement.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The parietal lobe is essential not only for spatial information but also numerical information .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h04","text":"The Temporal Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The temporal lobe , the lateral portion of each hemisphere, near the temples (Figure 3.22), is the primary cortical target","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The human temporal lobe— mainly the left temporal lobe for most people—is essential for speech.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The temporal lobe also contributes to complex aspects of vision, including perception of movement and recognition of faces and other objects.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When patients with schizophrenia report hallucinations, brain scans detect activity in the temporal lobes .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Frequent auditory hallucinations are related to thinner than average auditory cortex in the left temporal lobe .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Temporal lobe damage can lead to a set of behaviors known as the Klüver-Bucy syndrome .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The investigators who first described it reported that monkeys failed to display normal fears and anxieties after temporal lobe damage.","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Klüver-Bucy syndrome also occurs occasionally in humans after temporal lobe damage, where the most common symptoms are inappropriate sexual behaviors, overeating, and excessive lip-smacking or other mouth movements .","sourcePrintedPage":84,"sourcePdfPage":102,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h05","text":"The Frontal Lobe"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The frontal lobe , containing the primary motor cortex and the prefrontal cortex, extends from the central sulcus to the anterior limit of the brain (Figure 3.22).","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Its posterior portion, the precentral gyrus , is specialized for the control of fine movements, such as moving a finger.","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Each area along that gyrus controls one part of the body, mostly on the contralateral (opposite) side.","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most anterior portion of the frontal lobe is the prefrontal cortex .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, it occupies almost twice as high a percentage of the human brain as it does of a monkey brain .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Several areas in the prefrontal cortex and the temporoparietal junction have come to be known as the default network .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We often assume that daydreaming is unimportant, but it prepares us for decisions we might have to face later.","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The default network is also active when your brain replays recent experiences, an important process for storing memories .","sourcePrintedPage":85,"sourcePdfPage":103,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h06","text":"The Rise and Fall of Prefrontal Lobotomies"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Lobotomy began after a report in 1935 that damaging the prefrontal cortex of laboratory primates made them tamer without noticeably impairing their sensations or coordination.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A few physicians reasoned loosely—uh, very loosely—that the same operation might help people with severe psychiatric disorders.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In their defense, this was a time when psychiatrists had no effective treatment for severe disorders.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"His techniques were crude, even by the standards of the time, using such instruments as an electric drill and a metal pick.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Freeman began lobotomizing people with less serious problems, including some people whom we would consider mentally healthy by today’s standards.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When drug therapies became available in the mid-1950s, lobotomies quickly dropped out of favor.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Among the common consequences of prefrontal lobotomy were apathy, lack of initiative, memory disorders, distractibility, and a loss of emotional expressions .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with prefrontal damage often acted impulsively because they were unable to calculate adequately the probable outcomes of their behaviors.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h07","text":"Functions of the Prefrontal Cortex"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An analysis of thousands of studies concluded that the prefrontal cortex has three major regions .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The posterior portion is associated mostly with movement.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The middle zone pertains to cognitive control, emotional reactions, and certain aspects of memory.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After damage in this area, people can learn that stimulus A is better than B, and that B is better than C, but they might not infer that A is better than C.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They form memories, but they often don’t apply them to new situations .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The anterior zone of the prefrontal cortex is important for making decisions, evaluating which of several courses of action is likely to achieve the best outcome.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cells in the prefrontal cortex respond to these complex factors .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with prefrontal cortical damage often make decisions that seem impulsive, because they have difficulty weighing all the likely pros and cons.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h08","text":"Beyond Gray Matter: The Connections"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Historically, most researchers have concentrated more on the cell bodies (gray matter) than on the connections among them (white matter).","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, behavior and experience depend on the communication among cells, and that depends on the connections.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The Human Connectome Project is an effort to map all the long-distance connections, analogous to the way the human genome project mapped all the genes on the chromosomes.","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have already demonstrated many correlations between brain connections and behavioral tendencies, and they expect to find abnormal connections responsible for many psychological disorders .","sourcePrintedPage":86,"sourcePdfPage":104,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-2-h09","text":"How Do the Parts Work another.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even in vision, the area that responds to shape is separate from the area responsible for seeing the object’s color, the area detecting its movement, and the area detecting its location in space.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Karl Lashley noticed this problem long ago, but neuroscientists did not pay produce a perception of a single object is known as the binding problem , or large-scale integration problem.","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In an earlier era, researchers assumed that various kinds of sensory all information does not feed into a central “little person in the head.” Relatively few cells combine one sense with another .","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As part of this illusion, the visual stimulus alters the response of the auditory cortex, so that the sound really does seem to come from the same location as the dummy’s mouth .","sourcePrintedPage":87,"sourcePdfPage":105,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, if you watch a poorly dubbed foreignlanguage film, the lips do not brain.","sourcePrintedPage":88,"sourcePdfPage":106,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Its primary function seems to be one of elaborating sensory information and organizing sequences of behaviors.","sourcePrintedPage":88,"sourcePdfPage":106,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even fish, which have no cerebral cortex, can see and hear, but the cerebral cortex enables us to add great complexity.","sourcePrintedPage":88,"sourcePdfPage":106,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They’re lightly stimulate the postcentral gyrus, people report tingling sensations on the opposite side of the Inhibition is a genuine achievement: deciding not to act can require neural control as much as deciding to move."},{"question":"Can you explain: Avoid the localization trap?","answer":"It is useful to associate functions with brain areas, but it is inaccurate to claim that one small cortical patch uniquely contains a skill such as 'thinking' or 'personality.' the postcentral gyrus , or primary somatosensory cortex , receives sensations from touch receptors, muscle-stretch receptors, and joint receptors.","printedPage":83,"pdfPage":101,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":26},{"text":"Brain surgeons sometimes use only local anesthesia, anesthetizing the scalp but leaving the brain awake.","printedPage":83,"pdfPage":101,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":27},{"text":"Two of the bands receive mostly light-touch information, one receives deep-pressure information, and one receives a combination of both .","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":28},{"text":"Information about touch and body location is important not only for its own sake but also for interpreting visual and auditory information.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":29},{"text":"The parietal lobe monitors the information about eye, head, and body positions and passes it on to brain areas that control movement.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":30},{"text":"The parietal lobe is essential not only for spatial information but also numerical information .","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":31},{"text":"If during this process they lightly stimulate the postcentral gyrus, people report tingling sensations on the opposite side of the body.","printedPage":83,"pdfPage":101,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":95},{"text":"Separate areas along each band receive simultaneous information from different parts of the body, as illustrated in Figure 3.23a.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":96},{"text":"For example, if a person sees something in the upper-left portion of the visual field, their brain needs to know in which direction their eyes are turned, the position of their head, and the tilt of their body before it can determine the location of what they cortical target","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":33},{"text":"The human temporal lobe— mainly the left temporal lobe for most people—is essential for speech.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":34},{"text":"The temporal lobe also contributes to complex aspects of vision, including perception of movement and recognition of faces and other objects.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":35},{"text":"When patients with schizophrenia report hallucinations, brain scans detect activity in the temporal lobes .","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":36},{"text":"Frequent auditory hallucinations are related to thinner than average auditory cortex in the left temporal lobe .","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":37},{"text":"Temporal lobe damage can lead to a set of behaviors known as the Klüver-Bucy syndrome .","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":38},{"text":"The investigators who first described it reported that monkeys failed to display normal fears and anxieties after temporal lobe damage.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":39},{"text":"Klüver-Bucy syndrome also occurs occasionally in humans after temporal lobe damage, where the most common symptoms are inappropriate sexual behaviors, overeating, and excessive lip-smacking or other mouth movements .","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":40},{"text":"The temporal lobes are also important for emotional and motivational behaviors.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":98},{"text":"The area where the parietal lobe and the temporal lobe meet, close also to the occipital lobe, is the temporoparietal junction.","printedPage":84,"pdfPage":102,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":99},{"text":"This area apparently serves multiple functions, including attention, body awareness, and social cognition.","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":100},{"text":"Damage or disruption in this area, especially in the right hemisphere, impairs the ability to imagine how something would appear from someone else’s perspective.","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":101}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[{"term":"Temporal finger.","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":43},{"text":"Each area along that gyrus controls one part of the body, mostly on the contralateral (opposite) side.","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":44},{"text":"The most anterior portion of the frontal lobe is the prefrontal cortex .","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":45},{"text":"For example, it occupies almost twice as high a percentage of the human brain as it does of a monkey brain .","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":46},{"text":"Several areas in the prefrontal cortex and the temporoparietal junction have come to be known as the default network .","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":47},{"text":"We often assume that daydreaming is unimportant, but it prepares us for decisions we might have to face later.","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"The default network is also active when your brain replays recent experiences, an important process for storing memories .","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"Figure 3.23b depicts the traditional map of the precentral gyrus, also known as the primary motor cortex.","printedPage":85,"pdfPage":103,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":102},{"text":"Species with a larger cerebral cortex devote a larger percentage of it to the prefrontal the same operation might help people with severe psychiatric effective treatment for severe disorders.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":53},{"text":"His techniques were crude, even by the standards of the time, using such instruments as an electric drill and a metal pick.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":54},{"text":"Freeman began lobotomizing people with less serious problems, including some people whom we would consider mentally healthy by today’s standards.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":55},{"text":"When drug therapies became available in the mid-1950s, lobotomies quickly dropped out of favor.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":56},{"text":"Among the common consequences of prefrontal lobotomy were apathy, lack of initiative, memory disorders, distractibility, and a loss of emotional expressions .","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":57},{"text":"People with prefrontal damage often acted impulsively because they were unable to calculate adequately the probable outcomes of their behaviors.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":58},{"text":"In the late 1940s and early 1950s, at a time when legal and ethical restraints in medicine were lax, about 40,000 prefrontal lobotomies were performed in the United States, many of them by Walter Freeman, a medical doctor untrained in surgery.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":104},{"text":"(Freeman carried his equipment in his car, which he called his “lobotomobile.”) At first, Freeman and others limited the technique to people with severe schizophrenia, for which no effective treatment was available at the time.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":105}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[{"term":"Prefrontal regions .","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":60},{"text":"The posterior portion is associated mostly with movement.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":61},{"text":"The middle zone pertains to cognitive control, emotional reactions, and certain aspects of memory.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":62},{"text":"After damage in this area, people can learn that stimulus A is better than B, and that B is better than C, but they might not infer that A is better than C.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":63},{"text":"They form memories, but they often don’t apply them to new situations .","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":64},{"text":"The anterior zone of the prefrontal cortex is important for making decisions, evaluating which of several courses of action is likely to achieve the best outcome.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":65},{"text":"Cells in the prefrontal cortex respond to these complex factors .","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":66},{"text":"People with prefrontal cortical damage often make decisions that seem impulsive, because they have difficulty weighing all the likely pros and cons.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"When you decide whether to do something, you may consider the difficulty of the action, the probabilities of success and failure, and how valuable the possible reward would be to you, all things considered.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":106},{"text":"For example, the chance to win a pizza becomes less valuable if you have just finished a meal.","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":107}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[{"term":"Prefrontal .","printedPage":86,"pdfPage":104,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":72}],"originalFacts":4,"additionalFacts":0,"glossary":[{"term":"Gray another.","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":74},{"text":"Even in vision, the area that responds to shape is separate space.","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":75},{"text":"Karl Lashley noticed this problem long ago, but neuroscientists problem.","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":77},{"text":"In an earlier era, researchers assumed that various kinds of sensory information converge in areas that associate one sensation with person in the head.” Relatively few cells combine one sense with another .","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"As part of this illusion, the visual stimulus alters the response of the auditory cortex, so that the sound really does seem to come from the same location as the dummy’s mouth .","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"In contrast, if you watch a poorly dubbed foreignlanguage film, the lips.","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":81},{"text":"Applying these principles, researchers arranged a camera to video 3.25.","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":82},{"text":"So, the evidence indicates that we bind two experiences that that what you see is also what you feel and what you certain neurons in the posterior temporal cortex respond both when you see a chain saw and when you hear the sound it dummy’s mouth move at the same time, you perceive the sound as coming from the dummy.","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":112},{"text":"As you view the video of your back, it appears to be 2 meters in front of you.","printedPage":87,"pdfPage":105,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":113},{"text":"If you saw three flashes of light, you might think you heard three beeps.","printedPage":88,"pdfPage":106,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":114},{"text":"The near simultaneity of lights and sounds causes you to bind them and perceive an illusion that alters your perception of one or the Lamina IV, which receives sensory information, is prominent in the sensory areas of the cortex but absent from the motor cortex.","Lamina V, which sends long axons to the spinal cord, is thickest in the motor cortex.","Layer I, with many axons and dendrites but few cells, is a site for many connections, including those that are essential for learning. Ask whether a result identifies a necessary area, an area capable of producing an effect, or only a correlation. That distinction helps when reading the research described in later chapters."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-1","text":"Four broad research approaches"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers can examine effects of damage, stimulate a brain region, record activity, or relate anatomy to behavior across people and conditions. Lesions offer clues about necessity when a function is impaired after injury, though damage can affect connected networks. Stimulation can reveal what altering a structure makes possible or more likely, but unnatural activation does not necessarily reproduce normal function. Recording methods measure what happens during a behavior, often showing correlation without proving causation."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-2","text":"What recording methods actually measure"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Different instruments provide different information. Electrical recordings can track rapid changes with high temporal precision but may provide limited localization. Methods based on blood flow or metabolism offer useful spatial patterns but are indirect measures of neural activity and usually change more slowly. Anatomical imaging shows structures; functional imaging concerns changing activity. Do not interpret a bright spot on an image as a direct photograph of a thought."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-3","text":"Strengths, limitations, and triangulation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research designs differ in spatial resolution, temporal resolution, invasiveness, and the extent to which they can support causal conclusions. A technique that locates where something happens may be poor at showing when; a technique that records rapid events may make precise location difficult. Strong inferences emerge when multiple methods point toward the same explanation. Always identify the actual comparison group and the task the participants performed."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m3-3-study-4","text":"How to evaluate an empirical claim"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Ask five questions: What did the investigators manipulate? What did they measure? Was the result a relation or a causal test? Could the findings reflect other brain areas or wider networks? How well does the result generalize beyond the specific subjects and task? This habit will help throughout the book because virtually every later chapter relies on evidence from several methods."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h01","text":"Effects of Brain Damage"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This discovery revolutionized neurology, because it demonstrated for the first time that different brain areas have different functions.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Since then, researchers have made countless reports of behavioral impairments after brain damage.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain damage can impair the ability to recognize faces, to perceive motion, or to pay attention to the left side of the world.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although many interesting results come from people with brain damage, human studies have limitations.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Few people have damage confined to just one brain area, and each person’s pattern of brain damage is unique.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An ablation is the removal of a brain area, generally with a surgical knife.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"surface of the brain, researchers sometimes make a lesion , meaning damage, by means of a stereotaxic instrument , a device for the precise placement of electrodes in the brain (Figure 3.27).","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For comparison, the experimenter produces a sham lesion in a control group, performing all the same procedures except for passing the electrical current.","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"This procedure enables researchers to study behavior with a brain area active, then inactive, and then active again.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After any kind of brain damage or inactivation, the problem for psychologists is to specify the exact behavioral deficit.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h02","text":"Effects of Brain Stimulation"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The old-fashioned way is to insert an electrode into an animal’s brain and deliver brief, mild currents to an area.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That method has limited value, because the electrical current stimulates many types of neurons in an area, as well as the axons passing through.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A popular approach today is optogenetics , using light to control a limited population of neurons.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One protein reacts to light by opening a sodium channel, exciting the neuron, and another reacts by opening a chloride channel, producing inhibition.","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The second step was to develop viruses that insert one of these proteins into a certain type of neuron, or even to just one part","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Using these methods, an investigator can excite or inhibit a single type of neuron in a small brain area with millisecond accuracy, determining the function of cells in greater detail than ever before.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of the invasive nature of the method, it could be used in humans only when it might produce a medical benefit.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h03","text":"Recording Brain Activity"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During any behavior or experience, activity increases in some brain areas and decreases in others.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers modify the fish genetically so that proteins in the brain fluoresce when a neuron is active.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For many years, researchers relied on inserting an electrode to record activity from one neuron.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"New technologies enable researchers to use tiny electrodes that record from hundreds of neurons at once, without significantly interrupting normal function .","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Occasionally, researchers insert electrodes to record activity while a human brain is exposed preliminary to brain surgery.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The same device used for an EEG can also record brain activity in response to a stimulus, in which case we call the results evoked potentials or evoked responses .","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers using an MEG can identify the times when various brain areas respond and thereby trace a wave of brain activity from its origin to the other areas that process it .","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because the most active brain areas increase their intake of glucose, tracking the glucose identifies areas of increased activity.","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The computer uses this information to determine which areas have the most glucose, which are therefore the areas with greatest activity .","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For most purposes, researchers have replaced PET scans with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) , which is less expensive and less risky.","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An fMRI is a modified version based on hemoglobin (the blood protein that binds oxygen) instead of water.","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m3-3-h04","text":"Correlating Brain Anatomy with Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One of the first ways ever used for studying brain function sounds easy: Find someone with unusual behavior and then look for unusual features of the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the 1800s, Franz Gall observed some people with excellent verbal memories who had protruding eyes.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"He inferred that verbal memory depended on brain areas behind the eyes that had pushed the eyes forward.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"He assumed that bulges and depressions on their skull corresponded to the brain areas below them.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If people with a particular psychological strength or weakness share some unusual feature of the brain, then we can draw inferences about that brain area.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Phrenologists’ problems were, first, that the bumps on the skull don’t correlate reliably with the anatomy of the","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"brain beneath them, and second, that the phrenologists drew conclusions based on small numbers of people and analyzed their behavior only superficially.","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, to study the brain differences associated with normal behaviors, researchers would generally need large samples, probably a thousand or more, to get reliable results .","sourcePrintedPage":97,"sourcePdfPage":115,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, researchers reported correlations between the size of the amygdala Progress"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In any scientific field—indeed, any field of knowledge— progress almost always depends on improved measurement.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In astronomy, improvements in both ground-based and satellite-based astronomy have established conclusions that even science-fiction writers couldn’t have imagined.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Similarly, our understanding of the brain has advanced greatly because of the introduction of PET scans, fMRI, optogenetics, and other modern technologies.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Future progress will continue to depend on further improvements in measurement.","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary, at the end of this book.","sourcePrintedPage":99,"sourcePdfPage":117,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Certain unusual aspects of brain structure were observed in the brain of Albert Einstein .","sourcePrintedPage":99,"sourcePdfPage":117,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One interpretation is that he was born with certain specialized brain features that encouraged his scientific and intellectual abilities.","sourcePrintedPage":99,"sourcePdfPage":117,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Additional patients with speech impairments also exhibited damage in and around that area, now known as Broca’s area.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"The implications are deep: If you lose part of your brain, you lose part of your mind.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"By consulting a stereotaxic atlas (map) of a species’ brain, a researcher aims an electrode at the desired position relative to landmarks on the skull.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"The researcher anesthetizes an animal, drills a small hole in the skull, inserts the electrode (insulated except at the tip), lowers it to the target, and passes an electrical current to damage that area.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":91,"sourcePdfPage":109},{"type":"bullet","text":"Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), the application of magnetic stimulation to a portion of the scalp, stimulates neurons below the magnet if the stimulation is brief and mild, but with stronger stimulation it inactivates the neurons, producing a “virtual lesion” that outlasts the magnetic stimulation itself.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"If damaging a brain area makes an animal stop eating, you don’t know why.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h01","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"If brain damage impairs a behavior, stimulation should increase it.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"Development of this method required three steps, each of which would be useless without the others, and each of which seemed almost impossible.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"The first step was to discover or invent a protein that responds to light by producing an electrical current.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"Certain microbes produce such proteins, which researchers found ways to modify.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":92,"sourcePdfPage":110},{"type":"bullet","text":"The third step was to develop very thin optical fibers that can shine just the right amount of light onto neurons in a narrowly targeted area.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"This method demonstrated that one set of neurons responds while the fish hunts for food, another set responds while the fish swims to explore a new area, and yet another set controls transitions between hunting and exploring.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"To record brain activity in mammals, researchers use other methods.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"An electroencephalograph (EEG) records electrical activity of the brain through electrodes, ranging from just a few to more than a hundred, attached to the scalp.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"A magnetoencephalograph (MEG) is similar, but instead of measuring electrical activity, it measures the faint magnetic responses generated by brain activity.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"Positron-emission tomography (PET) provides a high-resolution image of activity in a living brain.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":93,"sourcePdfPage":111},{"type":"bullet","text":"PET scans use radioactive chemicals with a short half-life, made in a device called a cyclotron.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":94,"sourcePdfPage":112},{"type":"bullet","text":"An fMRI while you were, for example, reading would mean nothing without a comparison to something else.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":95,"sourcePdfPage":113},{"type":"bullet","text":"Researchers would record your brain activity while you were reading and during a comparison task, and then compare the brain activity for the two tasks.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":95,"sourcePdfPage":113},{"type":"bullet","text":"The results provide good evidence for general trends, but in most cases, they are not reliable enough to draw conclusions about an individual person.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":95,"sourcePdfPage":113},{"type":"bullet","text":"Gall then examined the skulls of people with other talents or personalities.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114},{"type":"bullet","text":"His process of relating skull anatomy to behavior is known as phrenology.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114},{"type":"bullet","text":"Today, researchers can examine detailed brain anatomy in living people.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114},{"type":"bullet","text":"One method is computerized axial tomography, better known as a CT or CAT scan.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":96,"sourcePdfPage":114},{"type":"bullet","text":"By measuring that energy, MRI devices form an image of the brain, such as the one in Figure 3.37.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":97,"sourcePdfPage":115},{"type":"bullet","text":"Researchers using these methods can relate behaviors to the sizes of brain areas.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":97,"sourcePdfPage":115},{"type":"bullet","text":"Weather prediction is vastly more accurate than it used to be.","headingId":"bp14-m3-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":98,"sourcePdfPage":116}],"topicIds":["bp14-m3-3-h01","bp14-m3-3-h02","bp14-m3-3-h03","bp14-m3-3-h04","bp14-m3-3-h05"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m3-3-study-1","title":"Four broad research approaches","text":"Researchers can examine effects of damage, stimulate a brain region, record activity, or relate anatomy to behavior across people and conditions. Lesions offer clues about necessity when a function is impaired after injury, though damage can affect connected networks. Stimulation can reveal what altering a structure makes possible or more likely, but unnatural activation does not necessarily reproduce normal function. Recording methods measure what happens during a behavior, often showing correlation without proving causation.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":91,"sourcePrintedEnd":102,"sourcePdfStart":109,"sourcePdfEnd":120},{"id":"bp14-m3-3-study-2","title":"What recording methods actually measure","text":"Different instruments provide different information. Electrical recordings can track rapid changes with high temporal precision but may provide limited localization. Methods based on blood flow or metabolism offer useful spatial patterns but are indirect measures of neural activity and usually change more slowly. Anatomical imaging shows structures; functional imaging concerns changing activity. Do not interpret a bright spot on an image as a direct photograph of a thought.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":91,"sourcePrintedEnd":102,"sourcePdfStart":109,"sourcePdfEnd":120},{"id":"bp14-m3-3-study-3","title":"Strengths, limitations, and triangulation","text":"Research designs differ in spatial resolution, temporal resolution, invasiveness, and the extent to which they can support causal conclusions. A technique that locates where something happens may be poor at showing when; a technique that records rapid events may make precise location difficult. Strong inferences emerge when multiple methods point toward the same explanation. What did they measure? Was the result a relation or a causal test? Could the findings reflect other brain areas or wider networks? How well does the result generalize beyond the specific subjects and task? 3.27).","printedPage":91,"pdfPage":109,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":17},{"text":"For comparison, the experimenter produces a sham lesion in a control group, performing all the same procedures except for passing the electrical current.","printedPage":91,"pdfPage":109,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":18},{"text":"This procedure enables researchers to study behavior with a brain area active, then inactive, and then active again.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":19},{"text":"After any kind of brain damage or inactivation, the problem for psychologists is to specify the exact behavioral deficit.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":20},{"text":"Additional patients with speech impairments also exhibited damage in and around that area, now known as Broca’s area.","printedPage":91,"pdfPage":109,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":59},{"text":"The implications are deep: If you lose part of your brain, you lose part of your mind.","printedPage":91,"pdfPage":109,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":60},{"text":"By consulting a stereotaxic atlas (map) of a species’ brain, a researcher aims an electrode at the desired position relative to landmarks on the skull.","printedPage":91,"pdfPage":109,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":61},{"text":"The researcher anesthetizes an animal, drills a small hole in the skull, inserts the electrode (insulated except at the tip), lowers it to the target, and passes an electrical current to damage that area.","printedPage":91,"pdfPage":109,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":62},{"text":"Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), the application of magnetic stimulation to a portion of the scalp, stimulates neurons below the magnet if the stimulation is brief and mild, but with stronger stimulation it inactivates the neurons, producing a “virtual lesion” that outlasts the magnetic stimulation itself.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":63},{"text":"If damaging a brain area makes an animal stop eating, you don’t know why.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":64}],"originalFacts":10,"additionalFacts":6,"glossary":[{"term":"Stereotaxic instrument","definition":"a device for the precise placement of electrodes in the brain","sourcePrintedPage":633,"sourcePdfPage":651},{"term":"Broca’s area","definition":"portion of the brain that is knife","sourcePrintedPage":618,"sourcePdfPage":636}],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":607,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":346},{"id":"bp14-m3-3-h02","title":"Effects of Brain Stimulation","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"facts":[{"text":"The old-fashioned way is to insert an electrode into an animal’s brain and deliver brief, mild currents to an area.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":22},{"text":"That method has limited value, because the electrical current stimulates many types of neurons in an area, as well as the axons passing through.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":23},{"text":"A popular approach today is optogenetics , using light to control a limited population of neurons.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":24},{"text":"One protein reacts to light by opening a sodium channel, exciting the neuron, and another reacts by opening a chloride channel, producing inhibition.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":25},{"text":"The second step was to develop viruses that insert one of these proteins into a certain type of neuron, or even to just one part","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":26},{"text":"Using these methods, an investigator can excite or inhibit a single type of neuron in a small brain area with millisecond accuracy, determining the function of cells in greater detail than ever before.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":27},{"text":"Because of the invasive nature of the method, it could be used in humans only when it might produce a medical benefit.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":28},{"text":"If brain damage impairs a behavior, stimulation should increase it.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":65},{"text":"Development of this method required three steps, each of which would be useless without the others, and each of which seemed almost impossible.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":66},{"text":"The first step was to discover or invent a protein that responds to light by producing an electrical current.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"Certain microbes produce such proteins, which researchers found ways to modify.","printedPage":92,"pdfPage":110,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"The third step was to develop very thin optical fibers that can shine just the right amount of light onto neurons in a narrowly targeted area.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":69}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":5,"glossary":[{"term":"Optogenetics","definition":"method of implanting a receptor into a neuron and stimulating it with light, to investigate the functions of a particular type of neuron","sourcePrintedPage":629,"sourcePdfPage":647}],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":294,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":252},{"id":"bp14-m3-3-h03","title":"Recording Brain Activity","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"facts":[{"text":"During any behavior or experience, activity increases in some brain areas and decreases in others.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":30},{"text":"Researchers modify the fish genetically so that proteins in the brain fluoresce when a neuron is active.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":31},{"text":"For many years, researchers relied on inserting an electrode to record activity from one neuron.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":32},{"text":"New technologies enable researchers to use tiny electrodes that record from hundreds of neurons at once, without significantly interrupting normal function .","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":33},{"text":"Occasionally, researchers insert electrodes to record activity while a human brain is exposed preliminary to brain surgery.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":34},{"text":"The same device used for an EEG can also record brain activity in response to a stimulus, in which case we call the results evoked potentials or evoked responses .","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":35},{"text":"Researchers using an MEG can identify the times when various brain areas respond and thereby trace a wave of brain activity from its origin to the other areas that process it .","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":36},{"text":"Because the most active brain areas increase their intake of glucose, tracking the glucose identifies areas of increased activity.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":37},{"text":"The computer uses this information to determine which areas have the most glucose, which are therefore the areas with greatest activity .","printedPage":94,"pdfPage":112,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":38},{"text":"For most purposes, researchers have replaced PET scans with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) , which is less expensive and less risky.","printedPage":94,"pdfPage":112,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":39},{"text":"An fMRI is a modified version based on hemoglobin (the blood protein that binds oxygen) instead of water.","printedPage":94,"pdfPage":112,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":40},{"text":"This method demonstrated that one set of neurons responds while the fish hunts for food, another set responds while the fish swims to explore a new area, and yet another set controls transitions between hunting and exploring.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"To record brain activity in mammals, researchers use other methods.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"An electroencephalograph (EEG) records electrical activity of the brain through electrodes, ranging from just a few to more than a hundred, attached to the scalp.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":72},{"text":"A magnetoencephalograph (MEG) is similar, but instead of measuring electrical activity, it measures the faint magnetic responses generated by brain activity.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":73},{"text":"Positron-emission tomography (PET) provides a high-resolution image of activity in a living brain.","printedPage":93,"pdfPage":111,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":74},{"text":"PET scans use radioactive chemicals with a short half-life, made in a device called a cyclotron.","printedPage":94,"pdfPage":112,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":75},{"text":"An fMRI while you were, for example, reading would mean nothing without a comparison to something else.","printedPage":95,"pdfPage":113,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":76},{"text":"Researchers would record your brain activity while you were reading and during a comparison task, and then compare the brain activity for the two tasks.","printedPage":95,"pdfPage":113,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":77},{"text":"The results provide good evidence for general trends, but in most cases, they are not reliable enough to draw conclusions about an individual person.","printedPage":95,"pdfPage":113,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":78}],"originalFacts":11,"additionalFacts":9,"glossary":[{"term":"Positron-emission tomography (PET)","definition":"method of mapping activity in a living brain by recording the emission of radioactivity from injected chemicals","sourcePrintedPage":630,"sourcePdfPage":648},{"term":"Magnetoencephalograph (MEG)","definition":"a device that measures the faint magnetic fields generated by brain activity","sourcePrintedPage":626,"sourcePdfPage":644},{"term":"Evoked potentials","definition":"electrical recordings on the scalp from brain activity in response to a stimulus","sourcePrintedPage":623,"sourcePdfPage":641},{"term":"Evoked responses","definition":"electrical recordings on the scalp from brain activity in response to a stimulus","sourcePrintedPage":623,"sourcePdfPage":641}],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":1029,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":417},{"id":"bp14-m3-3-h04","title":"Correlating Brain Anatomy with Behavior","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"facts":[{"text":"One of the first ways ever used for studying brain function sounds easy: Find someone with unusual behavior and then look for unusual features of the brain.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":42},{"text":"In the 1800s, Franz Gall observed some people with excellent verbal memories who had protruding eyes.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":43},{"text":"He inferred that verbal memory depended on brain areas behind the eyes that had pushed the eyes forward.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":44},{"text":"He assumed that bulges and depressions on their skull corresponded to the brain areas below them.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":45},{"text":"If people with a particular psychological strength or weakness share some unusual feature of the brain, then we can draw inferences about that brain area.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":46},{"text":"Phrenologists’ problems were, first, that the bumps on the skull don’t correlate reliably with the anatomy of the","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":47},{"text":"brain beneath them, and second, that the phrenologists drew conclusions based on small numbers of people and analyzed their behavior only superficially.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"However, to study the brain differences associated with normal behaviors, researchers would generally need large samples, probably a thousand or more, to get reliable results .","printedPage":97,"pdfPage":115,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"For example, researchers reported correlations between the size of the amygdala and people’s political orientation or their number of Facebook friends, based on small samples.","printedPage":97,"pdfPage":115,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":50},{"text":"Gall then examined the skulls of people with other talents or personalities.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"His process of relating skull anatomy to behavior is known as phrenology.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"Today, researchers can examine detailed brain anatomy in living people.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":81},{"text":"One method is computerized axial tomography, better known as a CT or CAT scan.","printedPage":96,"pdfPage":114,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":82},{"text":"By measuring that energy, MRI devices form an image of the brain, such as the one in Figure 3.37.","printedPage":97,"pdfPage":115,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"Researchers using these methods can relate behaviors to the sizes of brain areas.","printedPage":97,"pdfPage":115,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":84}],"originalFacts":9,"additionalFacts":6,"glossary":[{"term":"CAT book.","printedPage":99,"pdfPage":117,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":56},{"text":"Certain unusual aspects of brain structure were observed in the
