Few people have damage confined to just one brain area, and each person’s pattern of brain damage is unique.","An ablation is the removal of a brain area, generally with a surgical knife.","surface of the brain, researchers sometimes make a lesion, meaning damage, by means of a stereotaxic instrument, a device for the precise placement of electrodes in the brain (Figure 3.27).","For comparison, the experimenter produces a sham lesion in a control group, performing all the same procedures except for passing the electrical current. This procedure enables researchers to study behavior with a brain area active, then inactive, and then active again.","After any kind of brain damage or inactivation, the problem for psychologists is to specify the exact behavioral deficit.","The old-fashioned way is to insert an electrode into an animal’s brain and deliver brief, mild currents to an area.","That method has limited value, because the electrical current stimulates many types of neurons in an area, as well as the axons passing through.","A popular approach today is optogenetics, using light to control a limited population of neurons. One protein reacts to light by opening a sodium channel, exciting the neuron, and another reacts by opening a chloride channel, producing inhibition.","The second step was to develop viruses that insert one of these proteins into a certain type of neuron, or even to just one part","Using these methods, an investigator can excite or inhibit a single type of neuron in a small brain area with millisecond accuracy, determining the function of cells in greater detail than ever before. Because of the invasive nature of the method, it could be used in humans only when it might produce a medical benefit.","During any behavior or experience, activity increases in some brain areas and decreases in others.","Researchers modify the fish genetically so that proteins in the brain fluoresce when a neuron is active.","For many years, researchers relied on inserting an electrode to record activity from one neuron. New technologies enable researchers to use tiny electrodes that record from hundreds of neurons at once, without significantly interrupting normal function.","Occasionally, researchers insert electrodes to record activity while a human brain is exposed preliminary to brain surgery.","The same device used for an EEG can also record brain activity in response to a stimulus, in which case we call the results evoked potentials or evoked responses.","Researchers using an MEG can identify the times when various brain areas respond and thereby trace a wave of brain activity from its origin to the other areas that process it. Because the most active brain areas increase their intake of glucose, tracking the glucose identifies areas of increased activity.","The computer uses this information to determine which areas have the most glucose, which are therefore the areas with greatest activity. For most purposes, researchers have replaced PET scans with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), which is less expensive and less risky.","An fMRI is a modified version based on hemoglobin (the blood protein that binds oxygen) instead of water.","One of the first ways ever used for studying brain function sounds easy: Find someone with unusual behavior and then look for unusual features of the brain.","In the 1800s, Franz Gall observed some people with excellent verbal memories who had protruding eyes.","He inferred that verbal memory depended on brain areas behind the eyes that had pushed the eyes forward.","He assumed that bulges and depressions on their skull corresponded to the brain areas below them. If people with a particular psychological strength or weakness share some unusual feature of the brain, then we can draw inferences about that brain area.","Phrenologists’ problems were, first, that the bumps on the skull don’t correlate reliably with the anatomy of the","brain beneath them, and second, that the phrenologists drew conclusions based on small numbers of people and analyzed their behavior only superficially. However, to study the brain differences associated with normal behaviors, researchers would generally need large samples, probably a thousand or more, to get reliable results.","For example, researchers reported correlations between the size of the amygdala and people’s political orientation or their number of Facebook friends, based on small samples.","In any scientific field—indeed, any field of knowledge— progress almost always depends on improved measurement.","In astronomy, improvements in both ground-based and satellite-based astronomy have established conclusions that even science-fiction writers couldn’t have imagined.","Similarly, our understanding of the brain has advanced greatly because of the introduction of PET scans, fMRI, optogenetics, and other modern technologies. Future progress will continue to depend on further improvements in measurement.","They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary, at the end of this book.","Certain unusual aspects of brain structure were observed in the brain of Albert Einstein. One interpretation is that he was born with certain specialized brain features that encouraged his scientific and intellectual abilities."],"classroomResearch":{"title":"Evidence in context: Correlating Brain Anatomy with Behavior","body":"For example, researchers reported correlations between the size of the amygdala and people’s political orientation or their number of Facebook friends, based on small samples.","printedPages":[97],"pdfPages":[115],"kind":"textbook_selected_research","evidenceMethod":"single_verified_textbook_passage"},"classroomCoverage":{"status":"source_structured_full_book","level":"comprehensive_book_derived","topicHeadings":5,"bullets":23,"newWords":888,"allTopicsWithExplanations":true,"sourceScope":"verified_pdf_topic_facts_crosschecked_with_uploaded_markdown"}},{"id":"bp14-m4-1","chapterId":"bp14-ch04","moduleId":"bp14-m4-1","moduleNumber":"4.1","title":"Genetics and Evolution of Behavior","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":104,"printedEnd":116,"pdfStart":122,"pdfEnd":134,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Behavior reflects interacting genetic and environmental influences. Mendelian inheritance, sex-linked and sex-limited genes, genetic change, and epigenetics describe different ways biological differences arise."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heritability describes variation within a particular population; it does not mean a behavior cannot change with experience. Evolutionary explanations address how traits may have developed, but proposed adaptive explanations require careful evidence."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-1","text":"Genes, environments, and development"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Genes influence biological systems through the production and regulation of proteins. Mendelian inheritance describes how some traits are transmitted, but many behavioral characteristics involve multiple genes and environmental conditions. Sex-linked genes reside on sex chromosomes, while sex-limited effects can depend on bodily context. Mutations generate variation; changes in gene expression can also occur without changing DNA sequence. Epigenetic regulation concerns processes that influence how genes are expressed. It should not be treated as evidence that every experience rewrites DNA."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-2","text":"Understanding heritability correctly"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heritability estimates how much variation in a trait within a particular population and environment is statistically related to genetic variation. It does not tell us what fraction of one person's behavior was 'caused by genes,' nor does a high estimate make a characteristic unchangeable. When environments vary or populations differ, estimates can change. Genetic and environmental influences are not opposing percentages of a person; they interact during development."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-3","text":"Evolutionary reasoning"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evolution acts across generations when inherited variation influences survival or reproduction. A proposed evolutionary explanation of behavior must be assessed using evidence rather than assuming every trait is a perfectly optimized adaptation. Some characteristics are by-products, constraints, or consequences of changing environments. Evolutionary psychology asks how behavioral tendencies may have developed, but a plausible story is not proof. Distinguish a behavior's current function from its historical origins."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m4-1-study-4","text":"An exam-ready contrast"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mendelian genetics concerns patterns of inheritance; quantitative genetics often considers many genes and population variation; epigenetics concerns regulation of expression; evolutionary explanations consider changes across generations. Environmental modification can change how inherited tendencies appear. The correct study question is rarely 'nature or nurture?' It is how particular genetic, developmental, and situational influences jointly shape the outcome."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h01","text":"Mendelian Genetics"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mendel’s results demonstrated that inheritance occurs through genes , units of heredity that maintain their structural identity from one generation to another.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most genes come in pairs because they are aligned along chromosomes (strands of genes) that come in pairs.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An exception to this rule is that a male mammal has unpaired X and Y chromosomes.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Classically, a gene has been defined as part of a chromosome, which is composed of the double-stranded molecule deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) .","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes a genetic outcome depends on parts of two or more chromosomes.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It’s an amazingly simple code, considering the complexity of body structures and functions that result from it.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because each has one high taste sensitivity gene—let’s abbreviate it “T”—both parents readily taste PTC.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Therefore, a child in this family has a 25 percent chance of two T genes, a 50 percent chance of the heterozygous condition, and a 25 percent chance of being homozygous for the t gene.","sourcePrintedPage":105,"sourcePdfPage":123,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, an example like this can be misleading, because it implies that a single gene produces a single outcome.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have identified at least 10 genes that contribute to variations in eye color , and at least 700 genes that contribute to differences in people’s height .","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h02","text":"Sex-Linked and Sex-Limited Genes"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The genes on the sex chromosomes (designated X and Y in mammals) are known as sex-linked genes .","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"All other chromosomes are autosomal chromosomes, and their genes are known as autosomal genes .","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In mammals, a female has two X chromosomes, whereas a male has an X and a Y.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Psychological gender identification is another matter.) When biologists speak of sex-linked genes, they usually mean X-linked genes.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The small Y chromosome has a gene that causes the testes to form, but not as many genes as the X chromosome.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A man with the recessive form of this gene on his X chromosome is red-green color deficient because he has no other X chromosome.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Distinct from sex-linked genes are the sexlimited genes , present in both sexes but active mainly in one sex.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Both sexes have the genes, but sex hormones activate them in one sex and not the other, or one sex more than the other.","sourcePrintedPage":106,"sourcePdfPage":124,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h03","text":"Genetic Changes"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Changing a DNA base to any of the other three types means that the mutant gene will code for a protein with a different amino acid at one location in the molecule.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Given that evolution has already had eons to select the best makeup of each gene, most mutations are harmful, except when the environment changes.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, a mutation in a gene controlling the immune system might provide better protection against a new virus.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because some mutations occur as an embryo is developing or later, what we call “identical” twins can have genetic differences .","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because microduplications provide new material for genetic change, they have been a necessary part of our evolutionary history.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h04","text":"Epigenetics"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For psychology, the important aspect of epigenetics is that experiences can produce epigenetic changes, altering gene expression in the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Adding an acetyl group (COCH 3 ) to a histone tail loosens the histone’s grip on the DNA, facilitating the expression of the genes.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Removing an acetyl group tightens the histone’s grip on the DNA and silences the gene.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another epigenetic change is to add a methyl group (CH 3 ) at the beginning of a gene, turning it off, or removing a methyl group to turn it on .","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many experiences can alter the chemistry of the brain in a way that activates some genes and inactivates others.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Exposing a pregnant mouse to alcohol changes the brain epigenetics of her offspring .","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If a mother rat is malnourished during pregnancy, her offspring alter the expression of certain genes to conserve energy and adjust to a world in which food will presumably be hard to find.","sourcePrintedPage":107,"sourcePdfPage":125,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In humans, drug addiction produces epigenetic changes in the brain .","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Severe traumatic experiences in early childhood decrease methylation of many brain genes, increasing the later risk of depression or posttraumatic stress disorder .","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h05","text":"Heritability"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If the variation depends largely on genetic differences, the characteristic has high heritability .","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Heritability ranges from zero, indicating no genetic contribution to the variation, to one, indicating complete control.","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people call monozygotic twins “identical,” a misleading term because the twins can differ, sometimes because of mutations that happened after conception.","sourcePrintedPage":108,"sourcePdfPage":126,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the biological mother contributes not only her genes but also the prenatal environment.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A heritability estimate shows how much something depends on variations in heredity within a population, and it varies from one population to another.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If some families have strict rules and others are lenient, the environmental influence is stronger, and therefore heritability will be lower.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although a heritability estimate is interesting, it is more useful to know which genes are important for an outcome, and how those genes exert their effects.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because that approach tests a huge number of hypotheses at once (one for each gene), it has a risk of seeing an apparent effect by accident.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To avoid an accidental finding, the researchers need to set an unusually high standard for statistical significance, and therefore they need to test tens or hundreds of thousands of people.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h06","text":"Environmental Modification"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A prime example is phenylketonuria (FEE-nil-KEET-uhn-YOOR-ee-uh), or PKU , a genetic inability to metabolize the amino acid phenylalanine.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If PKU is not treated, phenylalanine accumulates to toxic levels, impairing brain development and leaving a child cognitively impaired, restless, and irritable.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although PKU is a hereditary condition, environmental interventions can modify it.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Physicians in many countries routinely test the level of phenylalanine or its metabolites in each baby’s blood.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If a baby has high levels, indicating PKU, physicians advise the parents to put the baby on a strict low-phenylalanine diet to protect the brain .","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People need to avoid meats, eggs, dairy products, grains, and especially aspartame (NutraSweet), which is 50 percent phenylalanine.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Physicians formerly believed that children with PKU could quit the diet after a few years.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even a genetically normal baby cannot handle the enormous amounts of phenylalanine that an affected mother might pass through the placenta or milk.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m4-1-h07","text":"How Genes Influence Behavior"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A gene can influence brain development, but it can influence behavior even without being expressed in the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":109,"sourcePdfPage":127,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If their reactions influence your personality, then your genes altered your behavior by altering your environment.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Now imagine a child born with genes promoting greater than average height and running speed.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of these factors, the child shows early success at basketball, and soon spends more and more time playing basketball.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As a result, the child spends less time than average on other pursuits—watching videos, playing chess, or anything else.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The point is that genes can influence behavior in roundabout ways.","sourcePrintedPage":110,"sourcePdfPage":128,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We should not be surprised that nearly
